title: A Father’s Strength
content:
A long silence followed.

The cold breeze continued to flow across the mountains as Siddu looked toward the distant horizon.

Then he finally spoke.

"After listening to everything Kiran told me..."

"I still couldn't accept it."

"I wanted to hear the truth from one last person."

"So..."

"I called Rohini."

"I asked her to promise that she wouldn't hide anything from me."

"I told her..."

"'No matter how painful it is... just tell me the truth.'"

Siddu lowered his eyes.

"She remained silent for a long time."

"I could hear her breathing."

"It felt as though she was struggling to find the right words."

"Finally..."

"She took a deep breath."

"And she confirmed everything."

"Everything Kiran had told me..."

"According to her..."

"...was true."

The words hung heavily in the air.

Sneha's eyes widened in disbelief.

"What...?"

"She betrayed you?"

Her voice trembled with shock.

Siddu smiled bitterly.

"It wasn't love..."

He looked away.

"She was only acting."

For a few moments, Sneha couldn't find the right words.

The cheerful, innocent love story she had been listening to had suddenly turned into something she had never imagined.

Finally, she gathered the courage to ask,

"What did you do after that?"

Siddu let out a slow breath.

"I broke."

"My world collapsed."

"I stopped talking to everyone."

"I didn't even call my parents."

"I didn't want anyone to know what I was going through."

"I simply locked everything inside me."

He smiled faintly.

"But Yashwanth..."

"He couldn't bear to see me like that."

"He knew I was destroying myself."

"So..."

"Without telling me..."

"He called my parents."

"And told them everything."

Two days later...

My father came to my college.

The moment I saw him standing outside the campus...

I was completely shocked.

He smiled gently.

Without asking any questions, he requested permission from the college and took me outside.

For a while...

Neither of us spoke.

As we walked together, he finally broke the silence.

"How are you, son?"

I forced a smile.

"Not bad."

He looked at me for a few seconds.

Then he smiled sadly.

"Don't try to hide it from me, Siddu."

"I'm your father."

I couldn't answer.

I simply lowered my head.

He understood everything without another word.

Instead of questioning me further, he took me to a nearby park.

It was peaceful.

The evening breeze carried the fragrance of fresh grass, while the warmth of the setting sun gently touched everything around us.

We sat together on an old wooden bench.

For a few moments...

Neither of us spoke.

Finally, my father gently placed his hand on my shoulder.

"Tell me everything, son."

"Don't keep your pain locked inside."

Those simple words broke something within me.

I threw my arms around him.

All the pain I had been carrying for months burst out at once.

I cried uncontrollably.

Every disappointment...

Every unanswered question...

Every sleepless night...

Every broken dream...

Flowed out with my tears.

My father didn't interrupt me.

He didn't ask me to stop crying.

He simply held me close, gently patting my back until my tears slowly came to an end.

After a long time...

I finally calmed down.

I wiped my eyes and quietly sat beside him.

He looked at me with the same warmth that only a father could have.

Then he spoke.

"Why are you crying, son?"

"If someone truly lost something today..."

"It's her."

"She lost a person who loved her with all his heart."

"You didn't lose your value."

"She failed to recognize it."

He paused for a moment.

"There's nothing wrong with crying for someone you truly loved."

"But don't spend your entire life crying over someone's betrayal."

"Think about your mother."

"Think about me."

"We love you more than anyone else in this world."

"If you destroy your life because of one person..."

"How do you think your mother and I will live?"

"Your happiness is our happiness."

"Your success is our greatest dream."

"So don't let someone else's mistakes decide your future."

He smiled.

"Focus on your career."

"Become the kind of man who earns respect wherever he goes."

"Become so successful that the world recognizes your worth."

"Be brave."

"Be strong."

"My son."

His words echoed deep inside my heart.

For the first time in months...

I felt a small ray of hope.

It didn't erase my pain.

But it gave me the strength to stand up again.

I looked at my father with gratitude.

"Thank you, Dad."

Those two words carried everything I couldn't express.

That evening...

I returned to college with a different heart.

The pain was still there.

But so was the determination to move forward.
